messages.content: Find an Italian restaurant near me in New York that provides vegetarian food options and a Japanese sushi restaurant in Los Angeles that offers delivery service.

function.name: restaurant_finder
function.description: Search for restaurants based on location, cuisine type and other preferences. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: City and state, e.g. New York, NY.

cuisine.description: Type of cuisine the user is interested in, e.g. Italian, Japanese etc.

preferences.description: Extra features in the restaurant. default is ['Delivery'].

message.reasoning:
The user wants two results:

1) An Italian restaurant near them (in NYC). They want vegetarian options.

2) A Japanese sushi restaurant in LA with delivery.

We need to call the function twice? The tool only accepts one request at a time; but we can combine into separate calls or maybe do multiple queries sequentially. We might have to use the same function twice because each query has different parameters. But the function signature expects city+state, cuisine, optional preferences array. For first: location="New York, NY", cuisine="Italian", preferences=["Vegetarian"]. Second: location="Los Angeles, CA"? Actually they didn't specify state abbreviation for LA; it's California. So location="Los Angeles, CA". Cuisine="Japanese Sushi"? Or just "Sushi"? We'll set cuisine="Japanese".

But note that the function's preference param is union type: either single string or array? It says preferences?: "Vegetarian" | "Delivery" | "Vegan" | "Takeout"[]. That seems ambiguous. Probably it should accept array of strings like ["Vegetarian"].

We'll produce two calls separately. Let's output JSON accordingly.
